## Trainer

Choose a **path** (the kind of music you know best), a **level** and a **question**. Then press **Start**: you hear the key
(a short cadence), then a progression on bass and piano. Answer with the buttons. **Space** plays it again, **Enter** checks or goes on.
Your settings and your last ten answers at each level stay in this browser.

<div id="harmony-ear"></div>

## The paths

Each path puts the same chords in a different order. Start with the one closest to the music you play or listen to.

| Path | Starts with | Comes late |
|---|---|---|
| **MLT (Gordon / Mullen)** | I and V7 in major, then minor, then IV; the modes (Dorian IV, Mixolydian ♭VII) | vi7, viiø7 and the diminished chords; **ii last of all** |
| **Rock and pop** | I–IV, I–V, three chords, ♭VII | ii and iii, borrowed chords (iv, ♭VI), the 12-bar blues |
| **Jazz** | **ii7–V7–Imaj7 from the first level** | turnarounds, secondary dominants, tritone substitutes, backdoor |
| **Classical (Hutchinson)** | cadences, predominants (ii and IV together), deceptive cadence | circle of fifths, secondary dominants, mixture, the Neapolitan |
| **Make your own** | the tonality and chords you tick | |

The MLT path follows Gordon: I V7 I first, then I IV I, then the two joined, then the same in harmonic minor before any more major
(*Learning Sequences in Music*, pp. 318–319). The subdominant in Dorian and vi (relative keys) are taught with them. Next come the seventh
chords on vi, vii and ♭VII, the diminished chords and the other modes, which he calls moderately difficult. Patterns with the
supertonic are held back until after all of these (p. 320). The rock, jazz and classical orders are this site's own. The classical
path follows the chapters of the theory text (see [Harmonic Progression](../theory/progressions.qmd)).

## The questions

They follow Gordon's four stages of readiness for hearing harmony. At stage 1 you don't notice that a chord changed. At stage 2 you
notice the change but not what kind it is. At stage 3 you know what kind it is. At stage 4 you can also guess what comes next
(*Learning Sequences in Music*, p. 305).

- **Did the chord change?** Two chords. Stage 2.
- **Name each function** (tonic, dominant, subdominant, subtonic…), **each bass note** in solfège (or the scale degrees or sargam chosen
  site-wide), or **each chord** as a Roman numeral. Stage 3. By default the first chord is given, as a starting point.
- **Same or different?** Two progressions, at most one chord apart.
- **What comes next?** You hear all but the last chord. Stage 4.
- **Which tonality?** On levels that mix major, minor or modes.
- **Inversions: the bass, then root or not.** Two steps a chord. First name the lowest note in solfège, then say whether it is the
  chord's root. With **Inversion step 2** set to *Root, 3rd, 5th or 7th*, say which chord member it is instead. The answer shows the
  book's figures (I6, I64, V65, V43, V42).

- **Follow a voice.** Name the note the soprano (or alto, tenor, bass: **Voice to follow** under *Sound and options*) sings in each
  chord, in solfège. Turn on **Bring out** for the same voice at first.

**▶ My answer** plays what you have entered so far, at any time, before or after checking. Empty boxes stay silent. Named functions
play the level's chord with that function. In *Inversions*, "Root" plays the chord with that root and "Not the root" puts your bass
under the real chord.

**Notation.** **♫ Show notation** (in the button bar, or *Notation* under *Sound and options*: hidden, after answering, always) draws the
exercise on a grand staff, exactly as voiced, with the notes lit as they sound. The Roman numerals, with inversion figures, appear under it
once you have answered. Each chord is spelled from its numeral (V7 in A minor has G♯), and the key signature is that of DO.

**Entering answers.** Tap the buttons: each fills the outlined box and moves to the next. Tap a filled box to empty it. On a computer
you can also type into the outlined box: numerals as written (`V7`, `ii`, `bVII`, `viio` for vii°, `viih7` for viiø7; capitals
matter), syllables (`do`, `so`), functions (`tonic`, `dom`…), `r` or `n` for root or not. An answer fills in as soon as only one
button fits. Otherwise press **Enter** (`V` waits, because `V7` also starts with V). **Backspace** undoes and **Space** plays it again.
There is no text box, so a phone never opens its keyboard.

Under the answer boxes, **▶ 1, ▶ 2…** play one chord at a time. Turn on **Bass alone** and they play only its bass note, which helps
with inversions. Before you answer *What comes next?*, the last chord has no button.

After each answer you see the progression, its key, its bass line in solfège and each chord's function. **↻ Again** plays it once
more. Ten answers with eight right marks a level as done; nothing is locked.

## Settings

Under **Sound and options**:

- **Voices.** *Three*: the bass and two notes above it (3rd and 7th of a seventh chord). *Four*: the bass and three above, voice-led
  like a chorale (the site's `satb.js`).
- **Key.** A random key each time, or one key.
- **Tempo** and **beats per chord**.
- **Silence between chords**: from none to 5 seconds after each chord, time to think or sing the bass. The chord's own length is
  still *beats per chord*.
- **Bring out**: one voice louder and the rest softer (soprano, alto, tenor or bass; with three voices: top, middle or bass), or a
  chord member wherever it lies (the root, 3rd, 5th or 7th). *The 3rd* is good for hearing major against minor.
- **Leave out**: drop one voice, to hear what the others do without it.
- **Arpeggiate**: play the notes of each chord together, rolled, up from the bass, or down from the top.
- **Pan the voices**: four voices S +50, A +20, T −20, B −50 (right is +); three voices top +50, middle 0, bass −50. With headphones,
  each voice has its own place.
- **Spacing**: voice-led (the smoothest motion, the default), close (upper voices within an octave) or open (wider than an octave).
  The **Close**, **Open** and **Voice-led** buttons under the answer replay the current exercise in that spacing without changing the setting.
- **Drone**: the resting tone (or the resting tone and its 5th) held low under the progression, to hear each chord against home.
- **Repeats**: with *Play each: twice*, the second time can be in a new key (with its own cadence first). You track the function,
  not the pitch.
- **First hearing**: at tempo, or the first play of each new question at half speed (replays at tempo).
- **Top voice sound**: give the soprano its own sound (the electric pianos or the organs) so its line stands out by colour as well as loudness.
- **Voice to follow**: for the *Follow a voice* question.
- **Notes**: held, or short and detached.
- **Chord register**: the upper voices an octave lower or higher (the bass stays).
- **Chords**: the length of progressions on levels that make their own (*Make your own*, and levels such as F2).
- **Establish the key**: a cadence, the tonic chord, or nothing (harder).
- **Inversions**: off (every chord in root position), some, or many. This works with every question: *Name each bass note* then asks
  for the real lowest note. The last chord always stays in root position.
- **Inversion step 2**: root or not, or which member.
- **First chord**: given, or you name it too.
- **Play each**: once or twice.
- **After answering**: wait, or go on by itself (hands-free on a bus).
- **Chords on** and **Bass on**: the band's piano sounds and bass sounds, or off. There are no drums.

The sounds load from the internet the first time, so start a session while you still have a signal.

## For teachers

- Bass in the band's bass, chords on the band's piano. Chords are in root position unless **Inversions** is on. Voicing is chosen for the smoothest motion;
  in four voices it follows `satb.js`'s rules. In three voices the rules are only nearest motion and the root in the bass, with no check for
  parallel fifths.
- Minor is harmonic minor in the MLT and classical paths (V7 has si). Aeolian uses ♭VII instead.
- Gordon has the class sing I IV V7 I in three parts: top so la so so, middle mi fa fa mi, bottom do do ti do. In minor: mi fa mi mi,
  do re re do, la la si la (*Learning Sequences in Music*, pp. 318–319). Three voices here is close to that, with the bass added under it.
- Saving to a class account (Supabase), singing answers into a microphone and more instruments are planned. The plan is in
  `research_notes/ear-training-plan.md`.
